title: Jason Cohen on expanding a plateaued $1M ARR SaaS into a new market segment
summary: Jason Cohen and Rob Walling coach the founder of Drop In Blog, a bootstrapped $1M ARR product that has plateaued, on moving upmarket. Jason covers delight versus table stakes, positioning around the buyer's personal stake, using ads to learn messaging, focusing on agencies and BigCommerce, and organizing the team around a new initiative.

principles.text: Utility and table stakes are not delight. Aim for something that makes buyers excited and talk about you to peers.
principles.quote: I'm hearing useful stuff, and that's great, but like, where's the part where they're excited?

principles.text: Position on the buyer's personal stake, like keeping their job, not only on features or utility.
principles.quote: If I'm a marketer at a big company and I want my job to not go away because big companies are in fact letting people go, aren't they? Like, you just save my job

principles.text: Don't let enterprise requirements erode the simple UX that made customers love you; add only the checkboxes you must.
principles.quote: If this is a strength of yours that it's simple and approachable and easy, you wouldn't want like, enterprise has lots of needs and demands of various sorts.

principles.text: Ads can be a temporary learning tool to find positioning fast, with a known budget, not only an ROI channel.
principles.quote: You can also think of ads instead of ROI to sale, you can think of it as, I'm gonna use this as a temporary tool.

principles.text: Focus on channels that compound, like agencies that bring multiple clients over time, plus the niche where you already win (BigCommerce).
principles.quote: Agencies is how you get multiple clients per year and therefore internal growth. And big commerce is is is your best single way of getting the big growth.

principles.text: Give each new strategic initiative a dedicated owner and separate revenue tracking, or the existing business will always trump it.
principles.quote: When you do a big initiative, someone has to be the owner and they're getting up and going to sleep thinking about only that.
